text:
Olivia: Heads-up — customer ACME wants a committed Redwood Dedicated GPU pool for their analytics pipelines. Sales asked for recommended commit sizing. They currently run ~120k tokens/min steady with 30k spikes and want 99th pct latency < 120ms.
Raj: Do we have their current model profile? seq length and batch behavior?
Olivia: Emily shared logs: mostly 1-2 prompt turns, avg seq=512, embedding calls rare. Throughput dominated by generation at temp=0.7.
Emily: Quick calc: on our A100-equivalent config, the steady 120k tokens/min ~= 2k tokens/sec. With avg token latency ~6ms per token single-GPU stream, that maps to ~12 concurrent streams? But batching changes it.
Raj: Can you drop the math? I want commit in GPU-hours/month for billing.
Emily: Sure — 2k tok/s * 3600s = 7.2M tok/hr. If a dedicated GPU does ~30M tok/hr (depends on kernel/quant/seq), then steady need ~= 0.24 GPUs. Spikes to 30k tok/min = 500 tok/s -> extra 0.017 GPUs. But need headroom and autoscale. Recommend reserving 1 GPU for baseline + burst pool, or commit 0.5 GPU equivalent with guaranteed warm capacity + burst credits.
Jordan (sales): Sales prefers chunky numbers customers understand: "1 x T4-equivalent slot" or "4k token/s committed". We need to map our internal GPU-equivalents to customer-facing throughput.
Olivia: For contracts, we bill by reserved capacity units (RCUs). Proposal: offer 1 RCU = 4k token/sec sustained (a conservative 90% SLO). ACME would need 1 RCU. Pricing team wants monthly GPU-hour estimate for finance.
Raj: Any billing oddities from last quarter we should surface? BillingBot: automated alert: "Detected 3 customers with committed capacity underutilization >70% last billing cycle; recommend reviewing RCU sizing guidance."
Emily: Actionable suggestion: add a "commit sizing calculator" in the onboarding flow that converts: avg tokens/min -> recommended RCUs -> GPU-hours/month -> estimated monthly commit price. Example snippet: 
```
input_tok_min = 120000
tok_per_sec = input_tok_min/60
rcu = math.ceil(tok_per_sec/4000)
```
Jordan (sales): Also flag region constraints — ACME wants eu-west-1. Our dedicated pool in eu-west-1 has fewer A100 slots, cold start lead time ~2 weeks for guaranteed capacity. We should include that in contract lead time.
Olivia: Agree. For contract language: "Committed throughput: 1 RCU (4k tok/s) in eu-west-1, effective on provisioning date. Warmup/scale policy: baseline 1 GPU-equivalent reserved, automatic burst to additional fleet up to 4 GPUs within 10s when available; fallback to cross-region with 500ms extra latency."
Raj: Sounds fine. Anything on cost optimization? Emily: Recommend offering 12/24-month discounts and overage token price tiers, but also provide advisory checks quarterly to rightsize. We can add a "commit utilization" dashboard so customers see % utilization vs committed RCUs.
Jordan (sales): I'll draft the term sheet with 1 RCU, 12-month, and a 15% discount. Note: confirm eu-west capacity with infra before sending. @Raj can you confirm?
Raj: I'll check capacity and cold-start timelines with infra team, and ping ops for reserve scheduling.
Olivia: Great — next steps: (1) Raj to confirm eu-west Dedicated pool capacity and lead time by EOD tomorrow, (2) Emily to prototype the sizing calculator and sample numbers, (3) Jordan to prep draft term sheet.
DevOps Bot: "Scheduled task created: check-dedicated-capacity-eu-west (due: 1718545523)"
BillingBot: "Created billing note: potential underutilization alert; recommend including 60-day trial credit for RCUs to smooth adoption."
Olivia: Thanks all — let's keep the commit conservative to avoid over-allocating GPUs yet meet ACME's latency SLO. Will follow up with a final recommended commit size after Raj's capacity check. :thumbsup:
